<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. 2	
3	This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8	
9	## Key Directories
10	
11	### Commands (`cmd/`)
12	
13	- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
14	- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
15	- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16	- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17	- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18	- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
19	- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20	- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21	- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22	
23	### Command Layout
24	
25	The CLI is organized around five noun groups plus a small set of top-level
26	verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb; legacy top-level
27	shortcuts remain functional but hidden, and emit a deprecation hint pointing
28	at the canonical group form.
29	
30	- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `stop`, `attach`, `resume`, `current`.
31	  `resume` with a branch arg switches to it and resumes its session; with no arg
32	  it opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions (across all worktrees),
33	  resolving each to its branch and pointing at the owning worktree when the
34	  branch is checked out elsewhere. Resume keeps an existing local session log
35	  as-is by default (`--force` overwrites it from the checkpoint).
36	- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `search`, plus
37	  the deprecated `rewind` (functional, prints a cobra deprecation message, will
38	  be removed in a future release)
39	- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
40	- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
41	  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
42	  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
43	- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `use`. `logout` takes
44	  `--everywhere` (revoke every session on the active core, not just the
45	  current one) and `--all-contexts` (log out of every saved login)
46	- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
47	
48	Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
49	`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
50	`configure`.
51	
52	Hidden top-level shortcuts (functional, emit a one-line deprecation hint):
53	`resume` → `session resume`, `attach` → `session attach`, `explain` →
54	`checkpoint explain`, `trace` → `doctor trace`.
55	Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
56	`checkpoint`. The `search` top-level remains hidden without a hint.
57	
58	Deprecated top-level commands (functional, print a cobra deprecation message):
59	`reset` → `clean`, and `rewind` (no replacement, announces removal — same
60	deprecation as `checkpoint rewind`).
61	
62	Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `trail`,
63	`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`.
64	
65	The `hideAsAlias(cmd, canonical)` helper in `cmd/entire/cli/aliascmd.go`
66	marks a command Hidden and sets cobra's `Deprecated` field so the hint
67	renders to stderr on every invocation while the command stays functional.
68	Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
69	`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
70	named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.
71	
72	## Tech Stack
73	
74	- Language: Go 1.26.x
75	- Build tool: mise, go modules
76	- Linting: golangci-lint
77	
78	## Development
79	
80	### Running Tests
81	
82	```bash
83	mise run test
84	```
85	
86	### Running Integration Tests
87	
88	```bash
89	mise run test:integration
90	```
91	
92	### Running All Tests (CI)
93	
94	```bash
95	mise run test:ci
96	```
97	
98	This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
99	
100	### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)
101	
102	The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls.
103	
104	```bash
105	mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
106	mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
107	```
108	
109	- **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
110	- **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
111	- **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
112	- Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
113	- The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
114	- **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.
115	
116	### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)
117	
118	**IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.
119	
120	```bash
121	mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
122	mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only as an example here, replace `claude-code` with other agents to run tests for those agents
123	```
124	
125	E2E tests:
126	
127	- Use the `//go:build e2e` build tag
128	- Located in `e2e/tests/`
129	- See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
130	- Test real agent interactions (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi, or Vogon creating files, committing, etc.)
131	- Validate checkpoint scenarios documented in `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md`
132	- Support multiple agents via `E2E_AGENT` env var (`claude-code`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`, `pi`, `vogon`)
133	
134	**Environment variables:**
135	
136	- `E2E_AGENT` - Agent to test with (default: `claude-code`)
137	- `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` - Claude model to use (default: `haiku` for cost efficiency)
138	- `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Timeout per prompt (default: `2m`)
139	
140	### Test Parallelization
141	
142	**Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).
143	
144	```go
145	func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
146	    t.Parallel()
147	    // ...
148	}
149	
150	// Integration tests with TestEnv
151	func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
152	    t.Parallel()
153	    env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
154	    // ...
155	}
156	```
157	
158	**Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.
159	
160	### Git in Tests
161	
162	**Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**
